issues.legal_issue: A village is unsettled on the date of resumption when no valid rent-rate settlement had been made applicable by that date, even if later rates are given retrospective effect.
material_facts: The rent-rate settlement made before resumption was quashed for failure to follow the prescribed procedure.
Replacement rent rates were fixed after resumption and were made retrospectively applicable from an earlier date.
The compensation authority used the replacement rates to treat the village as settled on the date of resumption.
issues.conclusion: The quashed settlement left no valid determination of rent rates, and the later rates did not make the village settled on the date of resumption. The village had to be treated as unsettled.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(n) and 6(3)(a)(i) of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Resumption of Jagirs Act, 1952, a village is settled for compensation purposes when rent rates determined in settlement operations have been made applicable. A settlement quashed for procedural invalidity leaves no valid determination. Section 86 of the Jaipur State Grants Land Tenures Act, 1947 permits rent to be payable from an earlier date, but retrospective rent realization is distinct from the prior effectuation of a valid settlement. No earlier judicial cases are relied on for this holding.

predicates.compensation_claim_on_resumption: A party sought compensation for property or rights taken on resumption.
predicates.valid_rent_rates_effective_before_resump: Valid rent rates from a settlement had been made applicable before the resumption took effect.

issues.definition: When compensation is claimed on resumption and no valid rent rates were effective beforehand, the village is treated as unsettled at resumption.

issues.legal_issue: A compensation right that vests on resumption cannot be altered by a later legal change unless the change expressly or by necessary implication provides for that result.
material_facts: The jagirdar became entitled to compensation on the date of resumption.
The compensation basis depended on whether the village was settled or unsettled on that date.
The later retrospective rates were fixed after the compensation right had vested, and the court found no indication in the relevant statutory provisions that the vested right was to be affected.
issues.conclusion: The compensation basis was fixed by the village's status on the date of resumption, and the later rates could not deprive the jagirdar of the vested right to compensation on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: A right to compensation vests on resumption. A subsequent amendment or change cannot deprive the holder of that vested right unless the law provides for that consequence expressly or by necessary implication. The court found no such indication in section 2(n) of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Resumption of Jagirs Act, 1952, or section 86 of the Jaipur State Grants Land Tenures Act, 1947. No earlier judicial cases are relied on for this holding.

predicates.compensation_claim_on_resumption: A party sought compensation for property or rights taken on resumption.
predicates.entitlement_vested_at_resumption: The claimant's entitlement to compensation arose when the resumption took effect.
predicates.later_law_lacks_clear_retroactive_intent: A later legal change did not expressly or by necessary implication provide for altering the already vested entitlement.

issues.definition: When compensation is claimed on resumption, the entitlement vests then, and a later change lacks clear retroactive intent, the compensation basis fixed at resumption is preserved.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for an unsettled village must be determined by reference to actual rental income rather than rates from a later settlement.
material_facts: The village was unsettled on the date of resumption because no valid rent-rate settlement had taken effect by then.
The compensation authority calculated compensation using rates fixed after resumption.
The governing compensation scheme provided a method based on actual rental income for an unsettled village.
issues.conclusion: Compensation had to be redetermined treating the village as unsettled and using actual rental income under section 7 of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Resumption of Jagirs Act, 1952.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Resumption of Jagirs Act, 1952 provides for compensation for an unsettled village to be assessed on actual rental income during the specified agricultural years. For a settled village, section 6(3)(a)(i), read with section 2(n), uses the applicable settlement rent rates. No earlier judicial cases are relied on for this holding.

predicates.resumption_compensation_proceeding: A proceeding determines compensation payable because property or rights were resumed.
predicates.village_unsettled_at_resumption: No valid rent-rate settlement had been made applicable to the village by the time of resumption.

issues.definition: In a resumption compensation proceeding, if the village was unsettled at resumption, compensation is based on actual rental income.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant whose compensation is remanded for redetermination is entitled to interest on the compensation from the date of resumption until payment.
material_facts: The court set aside the compensation orders and remanded the matter for fresh determination.
The compensation became payable on the date of resumption, and payment remained to be made after redetermination.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was entitled to interest at ten per cent per annum on the compensation as redetermined, from the date of resumption until payment.
issues.legal_principle: The court awarded interest as part of the relief accompanying the remand. It cited no separate statutory provision or earlier case, and stated no distinct doctrinal rationale for the interest award.

predicates.compensation_redetermination_ordered: A court set aside the compensation determination and ordered a fresh determination.
predicates.compensation_due_from_resumption: The claimant's entitlement to compensation arose when the resumption took effect.

issues.definition: When a fresh compensation determination is ordered and compensation was due from resumption, interest is payable until the compensation is paid.
